newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. pilot dies on Colombian anti-drug mission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pilot dies on Colombian anti-drug mission.

text.p: A U.S. pilot flying an anti-drug mission in Colombia was killed when his plane crashed in a jungle area of southeast Colombia on Tuesday, police said.
The pilot, whose identity was not released, was flying a U.S.-registered Turbo Thrush crop-dusting plane and was fumigating illict plantations of coca leaf, the raw material for cocaine.
He was believed to be the first U.S. pilot to die on such a mission in Colombia. The cause of the crash was not immediately known.

The crash occurred in a remote area of Guaviare province. The pilot was flying one of four planes on a spraying mission, and was one of six U.S. pilots operating in Colombia under a contract signed between the U.S. State Department and the Colombian government.
U.S. ambassador Myles Frechette said in a statement: "At this point we do not know what the cause of the crash was. The body has been recovered from a dense jungle area."

"The cause of the accident will be fully investigated and the U.S. Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) will have to get involved because it was a U.S. registered plane," Frechette added in his statement.

The U.S. embassy in November said U.S. pilots were flying missions to erradicate illegal drug plantations, which are often protected by leftist guerrillas or heavily armed gangs. It was not know whether any of the planes on Tuesday's mission had come under fire.
